findings.issue_text: Email reminders for cancelled bookings can still be sent because deleteScheduledEmailReminder only marks cancelled: true and the cron's cancel query filters scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour, so reminders scheduled in the gap between cron runs may be sent by SendGrid before any cancel is issued

Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget inside a forEach (not awaited) before the API responds, so on short-lived runtimes the process may be frozen/killed before cancel completes, and failed cancels are silently swallowed leaving the user seeing a successful cancellation
The cron's unscheduled reminders query may not filter on cancelled: true, so a booking cancelled between reminder creation and the next cron run risks its reminders being scheduled anyway

Dead try/catch around non-awaited forEach async calls in the reschedule block of handleNewBooking.ts: rejections are unhandled, the log.error branch is unreachable, and cancellation failures for rescheduled bookings are silently lost
One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the entire cancel batch in scheduleEmailReminders.ts because the try wraps the whole loop, skipping all remaining reminders including imminent ones that may be sent

Reschedule path with immediateDelete: true cancels at SendGrid but leaves stale reminder rows (scheduled: true, cancelled: false) with dead referenceIds that are never cleaned up and may be double-handled later

remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) fire-and-forget deletions in workflows.tsx are not awaited before the mutation continues, so completion of the mutation no longer implies old reminders are cancelled and may race with subsequent re-reads/recreates

Sender-ID configuration UI removed in WorkflowStepContainer.tsx (condition changed from isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded to isPhoneNumberNeeded), so steps needing a sender ID without a phone number can no longer be configured

Reminders with WorkflowMethods other than EMAIL and SMS on cancelled bookings are no longer cleaned up since the new code only handles EMAIL and SMS, leaving them to persist and be acted on by future schedulers
Serial per-reminder SendGrid cancel API calls inside a for loop in scheduleEmailReminders.ts cancellation sweep (N+1 shape); should be parallelized with concurrency cap or use SendGrid batched cancel

Unbounded findMany query in cancellation sweep missing take limit and missing scheduled/referenceId != null filters, materializing all cancelled reminders including unscheduled ones with referenceId: null

Sending batch_id: null to SendGrid for reminders with null referenceId errors and, being inside the same try block, a single bad row aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders and skips the deletion batch

Fire-and-forget async deleteScheduledEmailReminder calls in forEach loops in handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx, and workflows.tsx are never awaited or bounded, causing uncontrolled concurrent DB/network calls and silent loss of cancellations on process restart or connection close, leaving orphaned scheduled sends in SendGrid/Twilio
Migration adds cancelled column but no composite index supporting the recurring query pattern (cancelled = true AND scheduledDate <= X), causing full table scans on the WorkflowReminder table

Rescheduled/deleted bookings leave orphaned reminder rows: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true returns without deleting or soft-cancelling the DB row, and the cleanup cron only picks up rows with cancelled: true, so scheduled: true rows accumulate forever and may still fire reminders if the SendGrid call failed silently

Unawaited async side effects in cancel/reschedule handlers: fire-and-forget deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are never awaited, so on serverless/short-lived workers the process can exit before Twilio cancellation or DB deletion completes, and cancelled bookings may still receive reminders
Asymmetric SMS handling breaks the cancel-within-the-hour design: SMS manager deletes the row even when twilio.cancelSMS throws before the delete, leaving the row as scheduled: true and never retried

Cron error handling in scheduleEmailReminders.ts: remindersToCancel query lacks a referenceId != null check, so a cancelled row with null referenceId POSTs batch_id: null to SendGrid, throwing and aborting the loop, leaving remaining cancelled reminders unprocessed each run

Workflows needing only a sender ID lost their UI: the WorkflowStepContainer.tsx condition changed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only, so sender-ID-only workflows no longer render any configuration block

Useless try/catch around async forEach in handleNewBooking.ts: the forEach callbacks are async so the surrounding try/catch can never catch their rejections, making the log.error branch dead code and causing unhandled promise rejections

Package signature change on reminder managers: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder signatures changed from (referenceId: string) to (reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?), which will silently break out-of-tree consumers passing a referenceId string as the numeric reminderId

When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes the WorkflowReminder DB row, causing orphaned rows that remain scheduled: true and could be re-processed by other reminder logic (emailReminderManager.ts:197-215)

In handleCancelBooking.ts:484-494, deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder perform DB writes but are called inside forEach without await and excluded from Promise.all, so the request can return before cancellations are persisted and the email/SMS still fires

In handleNewBooking.ts:964-974, try/catch around a forEach of async calls is a no-op since forEach never propagates async rejections; the catch can never fire and failures become unhandled rejections, with inner managers also swallowing errors via console.log

In workflows.tsx, remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => …) drops the await on cancellation calls, so the tRPC handler responds before cancellations complete and failures are never retried while the user gets a success response

In scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-77, a single client.request failure throws out of the for loop, skipping cancellation of all subsequent reminders in that run, and within the 1-hour window reminders can hit their send time never having been cancelled

The deferred email cancellation design (mark cancelled: true, cancel SendGrid only within 1h) depends on the cron endpoint running; if it isn't invoked, cancelled reminders are still sent with no reconciliation/sweep for overdue cancelled reminders

For email with a referenceId on the non-immediate path, if the SendGrid cancel step fails the error is swallowed and the DB row is deleted anyway, so the scheduled email is still sent while the record of the failure is gone (handleCancelBooking.ts:484-494, bookings.tsx:484-493)

deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder swallow all errors with console.log, so callers cannot detect cancellation failure, with no retry, alerting, or proper logging with reminder id/referenceId context

In handleNewBooking reschedule, email reminders with immediateDelete=true persist with scheduled: true instead of being deleted or marked cancelled, making the reminder row state machine inconsistent between callers and causing noisy repeated cancel attempts on later reschedules

The migration adds nullable cancelled boolean with no default; pre-existing rows have cancelled = NULL and any future query filtering cancelled: false will miss them since Prisma does not treat null as false, a latent correctness trap

Duplicated reminder-cancellation logic copy-pasted across 5+ call sites (handleCancelBooking.ts:484-492, handleNewBooking.ts:964-974, bookings.tsx:484-491, workflows.tsx:208-215/372-381/514-521/569-578) with subtle variations in immediateDelete and awaiting; should extract a shared cancelWorkflowReminder helper

DB deletion of reminders is no longer awaited and errors are swallowed by try/catch with console.log inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder, causing DB writes to race with subsequent reads and failed deletes to silently leave zombie reminder rows; workflows.tsx:569-574 uses forEach(async ...) which never awaits
try/catch around forEach with async calls in handleNewBooking.ts:962-974 catches nothing because promises are discarded, making the error handling dead/misleading

scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-77 reimplements SendGrid scheduled_sends cancellation + DB delete instead of calling emailReminderManager, with divergent semantics (hard delete, 1-hour window heuristic), creating two inconsistent code paths

Ownership-scoping check silently dropped in workflows.tsx:~378 — previous deleteMany filtered by booking userId for per-user ownership, but new code deletes by id in reminder managers with no ownership check, allowing arbitrary reminder deletion

isSenderIdNeeded branch deleted in WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:387-389 — condition narrowed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded, possibly accidental feature deletion or leaving isSenderIdNeeded unused; should be verified
schema.prisma:644 cancelled Boolean? is nullable with no default false, so null rows from partial failures are indistinguishable from not-cancelled in queries like cancelled: true
Large whitespace-only reformat of test/preview code in workflows.tsx:~923-963 pollutes git blame and review; should revert formatting-only churn
Inconsistent error logging using console.log instead of log.error in emailReminderManager.ts:232, smsReminderManager.ts:188, and scheduleEmailReminders.ts:75 hides failures from monitoring

Unawaited async reminder cancellations at handleNewBooking.ts:964–974 and bookings.tsx:484–491: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called inside forEach without awaiting, making the try/catch dead code and causing unhandled promise rejections; transaction completes before reminders are cancelled and new booking reminders may be scheduled before old ones are cancelled

immediateDelete path in emailReminderManager.ts:206–219 cancels the SendGrid batch but neither sets cancelled=true nor deletes the WorkflowReminder row, leaving ghost 'scheduled' rows referencing the old booking (permanently inconsistent state in reschedule path, potential orphans in deleteWorkflow non-cascade path)

Cron cleanup in scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43–77 is best-effort and can double-send: cancelled reminders only cancelled at SendGrid within the next hour with failures only logged, and the catch wraps the entire loop so one SendGrid failure skips prisma.delete for already-cancelled reminders

SMS reminder deletion in smsReminderManager.ts:178–186 shares one try block for twilio.cancelSMS and prisma delete; if Twilio throws the row is never deleted and SMS has no retry mechanism (unlike email's mark-cancelled-and-retry design)

Lost authorization filter in workflows.tsx:372–385: replacement deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id) deletes by bare id with no ownership check, whereas the old deleteMany was scoped with booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }

New 'cancelled' column migration (migration.sql:2) is BOOLEAN nullable with no DEFAULT false or backfill, so existing and future rows get NULL, creating tri-state logic risk; NOT NULL DEFAULT false with backfill would be safer

Reminder cancellations in handleCancelBooking.ts:483–497 and bookings.tsx:484–495 are fire-and-forget: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls in a plain forEach are never awaited, so if the handler exits before microtasks complete, DB rows are never marked cancelled and the third-party scheduled send is never cancelled, silently sending reminders for cancelled bookings

immediateDelete branch of deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid batch but returns without deleting or updating the DB row, leaving rows with scheduled: true, cancelled: false, referenceId set that escape the cron cleanup (which only queries cancelled: true), causing permanently orphaned rows on every reschedule/workflow deletion

Race between cancellation and scheduler cron in scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43–78: cron fetches unscheduled reminders, cancellation deletes the row, cron then schedules the SendGrid send for the deleted reminder; the subsequent prisma update fails and the tracking row is gone, so the already-created scheduled send can never be found or cancelled — an unrecoverable reminder sent for a cancelled booking

Dead try/catch around a forEach of async functions in handleNewBooking.ts:962–973: the promises are discarded so the catch block can never catch anything, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection while giving the false impression failures are handled and logged

Edited workflow steps (workflows.tsx:~572–580, remindersToUpdate path) cancel email reminders with the non-immediate path that never reschedules with new content, so attendees receive the old reminder subject/body/time, while deleting a step uses immediateDelete: true — divergent behavior for the same operation class

Partial failure in the cron cancel loop (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53–77): a single failed client.request throws out of the for loop, skipping remaining reminders and discarding already-pushed prisma.delete promises, and a permanently failing cancel (bad referenceId) fails every run forever with only console.log and no alerting

SMS cancellation failure in smsReminderManager.ts:177–189 leaves the row live: Twilio cancel and prisma.delete share one try/catch, and since there is no SMS cron sweep and call sites are fire-and-forget, a transient Twilio failure means the SMS reminder still sends for a cancelled booking with no retry path

Authorization scope silently dropped in workflows.tsx:~373–383: reminder deletion now happens inside deleteScheduled*Reminder(reminder.id, ...) with no user scoping (previously deleteMany scoped by booking.userId), removing defense in depth if the upstream query broadens or the booking changes owner

Non-immediate email cancel never deletes the row for far-future reminders: rows marked cancelled: true are only deleted by the cron when scheduledDate is within the next hour, so a reminder 30 days out keeps a live-looking row for a month, and if the cron isn't invoked in that final hour the SendGrid send fires anyway with no backstop

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email reminders for cancelled bookings can still be sent because deleteScheduledEmailReminder only marks cancelled: true and the cron's cancel query filters scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour, so reminders scheduled in the gap between cron runs may be sent by SendGrid before any cancel is issued

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, cancelling a booking now calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete` (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`), and `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` then **only updates** the DB row to `{ cancelled: true }` rather than issuing the SendGrid cancel request (`emailReminderManager.ts`). Actual SendGrid cancellation is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only cancels reminders where `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. This creates a real timing/race concern: if the cron/API that runs `scheduleEmailReminders` doesn’t execute again before SendGrid’s scheduled send time, the reminder could still be sent. The diff doesn’t show the cron frequency, so the “can still be sent” outcome isn’t strictly provable from the diff alone, but the risk is directly implied by the new deferred-cancel logic and the 1-hour window filter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget inside a forEach (not awaited) before the API responds, so on short-lived runtimes the process may be frozen/killed before cancel completes, and failed cancels are silently swallowed leaving the user seeing a successful cancellation
The cron's unscheduled reminders query may not filter on cancelled: true, so a booking cancelled between reminder creation and the next cron run risks its reminders being scheduled anyway

adjudication.rationale:
In the new flow, when a booking is cancelled/rescheduled the code calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)`.
- If the reminder is *unscheduled* (i.e., no `referenceId` yet), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now **deletes the DB row immediately** (`if (!referenceId) await prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })`), so it cannot be picked up by the cron’s later “unscheduled reminders” query.
- If the reminder has a `referenceId` (i.e., it was already scheduled), the function does **not** make it “unscheduled”; it only marks `cancelled: true`, and such rows would not match an “unscheduled” query anyway.

Because the diff shows unscheduled reminders are removed on cancellation when they could otherwise be scheduled later, the specific risk described (cancelled between creation and next cron run causing scheduling anyway) is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead try/catch around non-awaited forEach async calls in the reschedule block of handleNewBooking.ts: rejections are unhandled, the log.error branch is unreachable, and cancellation failures for rescheduled bookings are silently lost

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the new reschedule block wraps a synchronous `workflowReminders.forEach(...)` in `try/catch` but calls async functions (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)`) without `await` or `Promise.all` (diff around `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach`). That means the outer `try/catch` will not catch async failures from those operations, making the `log.error(...)` path effectively useless for promise rejections. However, the specific claim that “rejections are unhandled” / “failures are silently lost” is not fully verifiable from the diff because both reminder-manager delete functions added/modified here internally `try/catch` and swallow errors via `console.log`, so they are unlikely to reject outward. This is still a concrete, diff-grounded review issue (misleading error handling / lack of awaiting), but not a clearly demonstrable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the entire cancel batch in scheduleEmailReminders.ts because the try wraps the whole loop, skipping all remaining reminders including imminent ones that may be sent

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts, the cancellation logic is wrapped in a single try/catch around the entire loop. Inside the loop, each reminder does `await client.request(...)`; if any one of these throws (e.g., a SendGrid/API error), control jumps to the catch and the loop stops, so remaining `remindersToCancel` are not processed/cancelled or deleted. This matches the finding that one failed cancel aborts the whole batch, potentially leaving imminent reminders uncancelled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reschedule path with immediateDelete: true cancels at SendGrid but leaves stale reminder rows (scheduled: true, cancelled: false) with dead referenceIds that are never cleaned up and may be double-handled later

adjudication.rationale: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` returns early when `immediateDelete` is true after cancelling at SendGrid, without deleting or updating the `WorkflowReminder` row (no `cancelled=true`, no delete). Call sites use `immediateDelete: true` in reschedule/delete paths (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` and `workflows.tsx`), and the later cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only deletes rows where `cancelled: true`, so these rows can remain stale with their original `scheduled`/`cancelled` values and referenceId.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) fire-and-forget deletions in workflows.tsx are not awaited before the mutation continues, so completion of the mutation no longer implies old reminders are cancelled and may race with subsequent re-reads/recreates

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the new code uses `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` (around the “cancel all workflow reminders from steps that were edited” comment). `Array.forEach` does not await async callbacks, and the calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are not awaited either. These functions perform Prisma writes (email: `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` or delete; SMS: `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)`), so the mutation can return/continue before cancellations are persisted, creating a real race where subsequent logic/re-reads/recreates can observe old reminders as not yet cancelled/deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sender-ID configuration UI removed in WorkflowStepContainer.tsx (condition changed from isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded to isPhoneNumberNeeded), so steps needing a sender ID without a phone number can no longer be configured

adjudication.rationale: In WorkflowStepContainer.tsx the wrapper that renders the configuration block was changed from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded` only. This means when `isSenderIdNeeded` is true but `isPhoneNumberNeeded` is false, the entire block will no longer render at all (previously it would). The diff shows this behavioral change directly, so sender-ID-only configuration states would become impossible to configure via this UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reminders with WorkflowMethods other than EMAIL and SMS on cancelled bookings are no longer cleaned up since the new code only handles EMAIL and SMS, leaving them to persist and be acted on by future schedulers

adjudication.rationale: Across multiple call sites (e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings router, workflows router), the previous unconditional DB cleanup (`prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id } })`) was removed, and the new logic only invokes cleanup functions inside `if (reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL) ... else if ... SMS`. For any `workflowReminders` whose `method` is neither EMAIL nor SMS, the diff shows no deletion/mark-cancelled path anymore, so those rows would now remain. The finding’s “future schedulers will act on them” part isn’t directly shown, but the missing cleanup for non-EMAIL/SMS methods is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Serial per-reminder SendGrid cancel API calls inside a for loop in scheduleEmailReminders.ts cancellation sweep (N+1 shape); should be parallelized with concurrency cap or use SendGrid batched cancel

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation sweep does `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) }`, which makes one SendGrid cancel request per reminder sequentially (serial N calls). This is a real performance/scalability concern introduced by the diff; it could be parallelized (optionally with a concurrency cap) or replaced with a more batched approach if available.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded findMany query in cancellation sweep missing take limit and missing scheduled/referenceId != null filters, materializing all cancelled reminders including unscheduled ones with referenceId: null

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation sweep does `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: now+1h }}})` with no `take`/pagination. This can pull an arbitrarily large set of rows (notably it’s `lte` with no lower bound, so it includes *all past* cancelled reminders too), which is a concrete performance/operational concern. The finding’s claim that it will include cancelled reminders with `referenceId: null`/unscheduled reminders is not directly supported by the diff (the only code path setting `cancelled: true` for email appears to require a non-null `referenceId`), but adding `referenceId != null`/`scheduled` filters would still be a reasonable defensive hardening.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sending batch_id: null to SendGrid for reminders with null referenceId errors and, being inside the same try block, a single bad row aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders and skips the deletion batch

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation loop calls SendGrid with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId` without checking for null/undefined (unlike prior code paths that gated on `referenceId`). If any `WorkflowReminder.referenceId` is null, this will send `batch_id: null` and can throw. Because the entire loop + `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is inside a single `try`, a single failing reminder aborts cancellation of remaining reminders and also skips executing the accumulated Prisma deletes (since deletes are only awaited after the loop).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fire-and-forget async deleteScheduledEmailReminder calls in forEach loops in handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx, and workflows.tsx are never awaited or bounded, causing uncontrolled concurrent DB/network calls and silent loss of cancellations on process restart or connection close, leaving orphaned scheduled sends in SendGrid/Twilio

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple async reminder-cancellation functions being called inside `forEach` loops without `await` or collecting promises. E.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts` now calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` and removes the prior `remindersToDelete` array and `Promise.all(...)` that ensured completion. Similarly, `bookings.tsx` and several places in `workflows.tsx` invoke these async functions in `forEach` without awaiting (and one uses `forEach(async ...)` without awaiting the resulting promises). Since `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` perform DB updates/deletes and external cancellation calls, not awaiting them can let the request/handler finish before these operations run/finish, dropping cancellations on early termination and potentially leaving scheduled sends/reminders orphaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration adds cancelled column but no composite index supporting the recurring query pattern (cancelled = true AND scheduledDate <= X), causing full table scans on the WorkflowReminder table

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new query in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` that filters `WorkflowReminder` by `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= ...` (`findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... }}})`). The migration adds the `cancelled` column, but the shown `schema.prisma` model change does not include any `@@index` on `cancelled`/`scheduledDate`, so this query could become inefficient on large tables. However, the diff does not definitively prove that no suitable index exists elsewhere (e.g., on `scheduledDate` already), so this is a performance/scalability concern rather than a verifiable correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rescheduled/deleted bookings leave orphaned reminder rows: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true returns without deleting or soft-cancelling the DB row, and the cleanup cron only picks up rows with cancelled: true, so scheduled: true rows accumulate forever and may still fire reminders if the SendGrid call failed silently

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)`, the `immediateDelete` branch cancels the SendGrid batch (`/v3/user/scheduled_sends` POST cancel) and then `return`s without either deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row or marking it `cancelled: true`. Call sites in this diff pass `immediateDelete: true` when deleting workflows/steps and rescheduling (`workflowsRouter` uses `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`; `handleNewBooking` does the same for `originalRescheduledBooking`). Separately, the new cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only fetches reminders with `cancelled: true` and then deletes those rows, so rows left by the `immediateDelete` path will not be cleaned up by that mechanism and can accumulate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unawaited async side effects in cancel/reschedule handlers: fire-and-forget deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are never awaited, so on serverless/short-lived workers the process can exit before Twilio cancellation or DB deletion completes, and cancelled bookings may still receive reminders

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple calls to async cancellation functions without awaiting them. Examples: `handleCancelBooking.ts` iterates `updatedBookings.forEach(... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) ...)` and never awaits; `handleNewBooking.ts` cancels previous reminders in a `forEach` inside a try block without await; `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` and `viewer/workflows.tsx` similarly call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` inside `forEach` without awaiting. Since these functions are `async` (changed in `emailReminderManager.ts` / `smsReminderManager.ts`) and perform DB writes / external cancellations, not awaiting them can lead to incomplete cancellation/deletion before the handler returns, especially in short-lived/serverless execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Asymmetric SMS handling breaks the cancel-within-the-hour design: SMS manager deletes the row even when twilio.cancelSMS throws before the delete, leaving the row as scheduled: true and never retried

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledSMSReminder wraps both `await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and the subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` in a single try/catch. If `twilio.cancelSMS` throws, execution skips the delete, so the row is *not* deleted (contrary to the finding’s claim). The statement that it “deletes the row even when twilio.cancelSMS throws before the delete” is directly contradicted by the control flow shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cron error handling in scheduleEmailReminders.ts: remindersToCancel query lacks a referenceId != null check, so a cancelled row with null referenceId POSTs batch_id: null to SendGrid, throwing and aborting the loop, leaving remaining cancelled reminders unprocessed each run

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cron block queries `workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: ... } })` without filtering out `referenceId: null`, yet it unconditionally calls SendGrid with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId` inside the loop. Since `referenceId` is typed/handled as nullable elsewhere in the diff (e.g., `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId: string | null, ...)`), a cancelled reminder row with `referenceId = null` would POST `batch_id: null` and likely throw. Because the whole loop is wrapped in a single `try { ... for (...) { await client.request(...) ... } } catch { ... }`, one failure aborts processing remaining reminders for that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Workflows needing only a sender ID lost their UI: the WorkflowStepContainer.tsx condition changed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only, so sender-ID-only workflows no longer render any configuration block

That means when `isSenderIdNeeded` is true but `isPhoneNumberNeeded` is false, this whole block will no longer render at all, removing any sender-ID-only configuration UI that previously depended on the wrapper being shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Useless try/catch around async forEach in handleNewBooking.ts: the forEach callbacks are async so the surrounding try/catch can never catch their rejections, making the log.error branch dead code and causing unhandled promise rejections

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the new block wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` in a try/catch, but the async functions `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are invoked without `await` (and `forEach` doesn’t aggregate promises). Any rejection from those async calls will occur after the synchronous try block completes, so the catch/log branch won’t reliably run and unhandled promise rejections are possible. The finding’s wording about an “async forEach callback” is imprecise, but the underlying issue is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Package signature change on reminder managers: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder signatures changed from (referenceId: string) to (reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?), which will silently break out-of-tree consumers passing a referenceId string as the numeric reminderId

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the exported signatures of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` from a single `referenceId: string` parameter to `(reminderId: number, referenceId: string | null, immediateDelete?)` in `emailReminderManager.ts` and `smsReminderManager.ts`. All in-repo call sites shown in the diff were updated accordingly, so no in-tree break is evident. However, this is an API-breaking change for any external/out-of-tree consumers that still call these functions with only a `referenceId` string; the diff provides no backward-compatible overload/wrapper, so it is a real review concern about package/public API compatibility (though out-of-tree impact can’t be verified from the diff alone).

adjudication_records.issue_text: When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes the WorkflowReminder DB row, causing orphaned rows that remain scheduled: true and could be re-processed by other reminder logic (emailReminderManager.ts:197-215)

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` returns early when `immediateDelete` is true after canceling the SendGrid batch (`/v3/user/scheduled_sends` POST with status `cancel`) and does not delete or update the corresponding `WorkflowReminder` row (no `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` / `update`). adjudication_records.issue_text: In handleCancelBooking.ts:484-494, deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder perform DB writes but are called inside forEach without await and excluded from Promise.all, so the request can return before cancellations are persisted and the email/SMS still fires

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the diff replaces collecting Prisma delete promises with direct calls to async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside nested forEach loops, but those calls are not awaited and are not included in prismaPromises/Promise.all (prismaPromises is now only [attendeeDeletes, bookingReferenceDeletes]). The called functions perform DB writes (emailReminderManager.ts updates/deletes WorkflowReminder; smsReminderManager.ts deletes WorkflowReminder and may call Twilio), so the handler can complete before these cancellations persist, potentially allowing reminders to still fire or leaving inconsistent state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In handleNewBooking.ts:964-974, try/catch around a forEach of async calls is a no-op since forEach never propagates async rejections; the catch can never fire and failures become unhandled rejections, with inner managers also swallowing errors via console.log

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the new block wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` in a try/catch but calls async `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` without awaiting or collecting promises, so the try/catch won’t observe async failures. However, in this diff both manager functions already internally catch and `console.log` errors (they don’t rethrow), so the finding’s claim about “unhandled rejections”/catch “can never fire” is overstated; the practical issue is ineffective outer error handling and non-awaited cancellation work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In workflows.tsx, remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => …) drops the await on cancellation calls, so the tRPC handler responds before cancellations complete and failures are never retried while the user gets a success response

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the diff introduces `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... })` without collecting/awaiting the resulting promises. Additionally, the cancellation functions `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are `async` and are called without `await` inside that callback. This means the handler can continue (and ultimately return success) before the DB updates/deletes and external cancellations complete, and any rejection would be unobserved by the caller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-77, a single client.request failure throws out of the for loop, skipping cancellation of all subsequent reminders in that run, and within the 1-hour window reminders can hit their send time never having been cancelled

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts, the entire cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch (new block around lines ~40-75). Inside the `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop, each iteration does an `await client.request(...)`. If any one `client.request` throws, execution jumps to the catch and the loop aborts, so subsequent reminders in `remindersToCancel` are not cancelled/deleted in that run. Given this job targets reminders scheduled within the next hour, this can leave later reminders uncancelled until a future run (or ever), allowing them to reach send time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The deferred email cancellation design (mark cancelled: true, cancel SendGrid only within 1h) depends on the cron endpoint running; if it isn't invoked, cancelled reminders are still sent with no reconciliation/sweep for overdue cancelled reminders

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` no longer cancels the SendGrid scheduled send for the common path; it just marks the DB row `cancelled: true` (`emailReminderManager.ts` updates the reminder unless `immediateDelete` is passed). Actual SendGrid cancellation + DB deletion is only performed in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which queries `WorkflowReminder` rows where `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h` and then posts `status: "cancel"` to SendGrid. So cancellation correctness depends on that API/cron running; if it doesn’t run, the SendGrid scheduled send is not cancelled and could still go out. This is a diff-grounded design/operational risk rather than a directly provable defect in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: For email with a referenceId on the non-immediate path, if the SendGrid cancel step fails the error is swallowed and the DB row is deleted anyway, so the scheduled email is still sent while the record of the failure is gone (handleCancelBooking.ts:484-494, bookings.tsx:484-493)

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, the non-immediate email cancellation path does not attempt a SendGrid cancel and does not delete the DB row. `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `bookings.tsx` call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete`. In `emailReminderManager.ts`, when `referenceId` is present and `immediateDelete` is falsy, it only runs `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })` and returns; it does not delete the row. Therefore the claimed behavior (“SendGrid cancel fails, error swallowed, DB row deleted anyway, scheduled email still sent while failure record is gone”) is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder swallow all errors with console.log, so callers cannot detect cancellation failure, with no retry, alerting, or proper logging with reminder id/referenceId context

In handleNewBooking reschedule, email reminders with immediateDelete=true persist with scheduled: true instead of being deleted or marked cancelled, making the reminder row state machine inconsistent between callers and causing noisy repeated cancel attempts on later reschedules

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking` reschedule logic, email reminders are cancelled via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`. In `emailReminderManager.ts`, the `immediateDelete` branch only POSTs a cancel to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` and then `return`s without updating or deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row. Thus the DB row can remain with `scheduled: true` (and no `cancelled` flag set), unlike the non-immediate path which sets `cancelled: true`, and unlike SMS which always deletes the row. This inconsistency can lead to repeated later cancellation attempts because the reminder record persists in a scheduled-looking state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The migration adds nullable cancelled boolean with no default; pre-existing rows have cancelled = NULL and any future query filtering cancelled: false will miss them since Prisma does not treat null as false, a latent correctness trap
matched_golden_ids: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify that the `cancelled` column is created as nullable without a default, leading to existing rows having NULL instead of false and causing incorrect behavior in queries/checks that expect false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated reminder-cancellation logic copy-pasted across 5+ call sites (handleCancelBooking.ts:484-492, handleNewBooking.ts:964-974, bookings.tsx:484-491, workflows.tsx:208-215/372-381/514-521/569-578) with subtle variations in immediateDelete and awaiting; should extract a shared cancelWorkflowReminder helper

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB deletion of reminders is no longer awaited and errors are swallowed by try/catch with console.log inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder, causing DB writes to race with subsequent reads and failed deletes to silently leave zombie reminder rows; workflows.tsx:569-574 uses forEach(async ...) which never awaits

adjudication.rationale: In multiple places the diff replaces awaited Prisma deletions with calls to async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder that are not awaited (e.g., handleCancelBooking.ts removes remindersToDelete + Promise.all; bookings.tsx similarly removes Promise.all(remindersToDelete); workflows.tsx calls deleteScheduled* inside forEach without collecting/awaiting promises). Those reminder-manager functions perform Prisma writes (workflowReminder.delete/update/delete) but catch and only console.log errors, so failures become silent and the lack of awaiting can cause these DB writes/cancels to race or not complete before the request finishes (especially in serverless). adjudication_records.issue_text: try/catch around forEach with async calls in handleNewBooking.ts:962-974 catches nothing because promises are discarded, making the error handling dead/misleading

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the new try/catch wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` but the body calls async functions (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)`) without `await`/`Promise.all`. Any rejection from those promises would not be caught by this try/catch (it only catches synchronous exceptions), so the logging suggests protection that isn’t actually provided. This is misleading error handling and also means cancellation isn’t guaranteed to finish before the reschedule continues, even though the underlying delete functions currently have their own internal try/catch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-77 reimplements SendGrid scheduled_sends cancellation + DB delete instead of calling emailReminderManager, with divergent semantics (hard delete, 1-hour window heuristic), creating two inconsistent code paths

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts` a new block (after creating the SendGrid client) directly calls `client.request` to cancel scheduled_sends and then hard-deletes `workflowReminder` rows (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete`) for reminders with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`. This duplicates logic that now exists in `emailReminderManager.deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)`, but with different semantics: the manager path typically marks `cancelled: true` (or cancels and returns early on `immediateDelete`) rather than always deleting, and it doesn’t implement the same 1-hour window. adjudication_records.issue_text: Ownership-scoping check silently dropped in workflows.tsx:~378 — previous deleteMany filtered by booking userId for per-user ownership, but new code deletes by id in reminder managers with no ownership check, allowing arbitrary reminder deletion

adjudication_records.issue_text: isSenderIdNeeded branch deleted in WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:387-389 — condition narrowed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded, possibly accidental feature deletion or leaving isSenderIdNeeded unused; should be verified

adjudication_records.issue_text: schema.prisma:644 cancelled Boolean? is nullable with no default false, so null rows from partial failures are indistinguishable from not-cancelled in queries like cancelled: true

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `cancelled Boolean?` in `schema.prisma` and a migration that creates a nullable `BOOLEAN` column with no default. New logic relies on `cancelled: true` filtering (e.g., `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` queries `where: { cancelled: true, ... }` and `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` sets `cancelled: true`). Allowing `null` creates an unnecessary tri-state where `null` and `false` are both treated as “not cancelled” by these queries, which can complicate semantics and future queries (e.g., `cancelled: false` would not match existing `null` rows). This is a schema/edge-case design concern grounded in the diff, but not a directly verifiable functional defect from the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent error logging using console.log instead of log.error in emailReminderManager.ts:232, smsReminderManager.ts:188, and scheduleEmailReminders.ts:75 hides failures from monitoring

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cron cleanup in scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43–77 is best-effort and can double-send: cancelled reminders only cancelled at SendGrid within the next hour with failures only logged, and the catch wraps the entire loop so one SendGrid failure skips prisma.delete for already-cancelled reminders

adjudication_records.issue_text: SMS reminder deletion in smsReminderManager.ts:178–186 shares one try block for twilio.cancelSMS and prisma delete; if Twilio throws the row is never deleted and SMS has no retry mechanism (unlike email's mark-cancelled-and-retry design)

adjudication_records.issue_text: New 'cancelled' column migration (migration.sql:2) is BOOLEAN nullable with no DEFAULT false or backfill, so existing and future rows get NULL, creating tri-state logic risk; NOT NULL DEFAULT false with backfill would be safer

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `cancelled` as a nullable boolean (`ALTER TABLE "WorkflowReminder" ADD COLUMN "cancelled" BOOLEAN;` and `cancelled Boolean?` in `schema.prisma`) with no default/backfill. New code relies on `cancelled: true` queries (e.g. `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` findMany where `cancelled: true`) and sets it via `update({ data: { cancelled: true }})` in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`. While this doesn't immediately break current logic (NULL rows simply won't match `cancelled: true`), it does introduce a tri-state field that can cause subtle behavior differences if any code later queries `cancelled: false` (which would not match NULL) or assumes non-null semantics. Making it `NOT NULL DEFAULT false` with backfill would be safer and clearer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reminder cancellations in handleCancelBooking.ts:483–497 and bookings.tsx:484–495 are fire-and-forget: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls in a plain forEach are never awaited, so if the handler exits before microtasks complete, DB rows are never marked cancelled and the third-party scheduled send is never cancelled, silently sending reminders for cancelled bookings

adjudication.rationale: In both `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `bookings.tsx`, the diff replaces Prisma deletion batching with direct calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` inside `forEach` loops, but these functions are `async` (see `emailReminderManager.ts` / `smsReminderManager.ts`) and the calls are not `await`ed or collected into a `Promise.all`. In `handleCancelBooking.ts` specifically, `prismaPromises` no longer includes reminder operations, so the handler only awaits attendee/bookingReference deletes and `apiDeletes`, not the reminder cancellations. As a result, reminder DB updates/deletes (e.g., marking `cancelled: true` for email) and third-party cancels can be left incomplete if the request finishes/tears down early.

adjudication_records.issue_text: immediateDelete branch of deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid batch but returns without deleting or updating the DB row, leaving rows with scheduled: true, cancelled: false, referenceId set that escape the cron cleanup (which only queries cancelled: true), causing permanently orphaned rows on every reschedule/workflow deletion

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race between cancellation and scheduler cron in scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43–78: cron fetches unscheduled reminders, cancellation deletes the row, cron then schedules the SendGrid send for the deleted reminder; the subsequent prisma update fails and the tracking row is gone, so the already-created scheduled send can never be found or cancelled — an unrecoverable reminder sent for a cancelled booking

Any concurrency race with other processes is plausible in general, but it isn’t verifiable from this diff, and the described ordering contradicts the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead try/catch around a forEach of async functions in handleNewBooking.ts:962–973: the promises are discarded so the catch block can never catch anything, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection while giving the false impression failures are handled and logged

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the newly added block `try { originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); }); } catch { ... }` calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without `await` or collecting promises. Both functions are `async` (see emailReminderManager.ts and smsReminderManager.ts), so any rejection happens asynchronously and will not be caught by the surrounding synchronous try/catch, potentially becoming an unhandled promise rejection while logging implies errors are handled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Edited workflow steps (workflows.tsx:~572–580, remindersToUpdate path) cancel email reminders with the non-immediate path that never reschedules with new content, so attendees receive the old reminder subject/body/time, while deleting a step uses immediateDelete: true — divergent behavior for the same operation class

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows divergent cancellation semantics for EMAIL reminders depending on operation: deleting a step/workflow calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` (immediate remote cancel), while editing steps uses `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` (non-immediate), which in `emailReminderManager.ts` only marks the DB row `cancelled: true` and does not cancel the external scheduled send. Actual remote cancellation/deletion is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only cancels `cancelled=true` reminders with `scheduledDate <= now+1h`. So the finding’s “divergent behavior” part is verifiable; however, the claim that attendees will “receive the old reminder” / “never reschedules” is not directly provable from this diff (it depends on external scheduling cadence and rescheduling logic not shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial failure in the cron cancel loop (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53–77): a single failed client.request throws out of the for loop, skipping remaining reminders and discarding already-pushed prisma.delete promises, and a permanently failing cancel (bad referenceId) fails every run forever with only console.log and no alerting

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` in a single `try/catch`. Because each iteration does `await client.request(...)`, one thrown error aborts the whole loop and jumps to `catch`, so remaining reminders are skipped. Also, `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls are only pushed into `workflowRemindersToDelete` and executed via `await Promise.all(...)` after the loop; if an error occurs mid-loop, that `Promise.all` is never reached, so already-prepared deletes are never awaited/executed (Prisma queries are lazy until awaited). Finally, a reminder with a bad `referenceId` will keep matching the query (`cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`) and will be retried every run, with only `console.log` and no state change to prevent repeated failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SMS cancellation failure in smsReminderManager.ts:177–189 leaves the row live: Twilio cancel and prisma.delete share one try/catch, and since there is no SMS cron sweep and call sites are fire-and-forget, a transient Twilio failure means the SMS reminder still sends for a cancelled booking with no retry path

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId) wraps both `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })` in a single try/catch. If Twilio cancellation throws (transient API failure), the Prisma delete is skipped and the reminder row remains. Multiple new call sites invoke this function without `await` (e.g., handleCancelBooking.ts, viewer/bookings.tsx, viewer/workflows.tsx use `forEach` and don't await), so failures are effectively fire-and-forget with no visible retry/cleanup path in this diff. This can leave cancelled/rescheduled bookings with still-scheduled SMS (since Twilio cancel did not succeed) and an undeleted DB reminder record.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization scope silently dropped in workflows.tsx:~373–383: reminder deletion now happens inside deleteScheduled*Reminder(reminder.id, ...) with no user scoping (previously deleteMany scoped by booking.userId), removing defense in depth if the upstream query broadens or the booking changes owner

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` the diff removes the explicit, user-scoped DB delete (`ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})`) and now only calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)`, which (per the diff) update/delete by `id` without any `ctx.user.id`/booking ownership constraint. The finding’s “defense in depth dropped” claim is directly supported by the change, though whether it is exploitable depends on upstream query scoping not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-immediate email cancel never deletes the row for far-future reminders: rows marked cancelled: true are only deleted by the cron when scheduledDate is within the next hour, so a reminder 30 days out keeps a live-looking row for a month, and if the cron isn't invoked in that final hour the SendGrid send fires anyway with no backstop

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, non-immediate email cancellation no longer cancels the SendGrid scheduled send and does not delete the DB row. Specifically, callers like `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `bookings.tsx` now call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete`, and `emailReminderManager.deleteScheduledEmailReminder` in that case only does `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` and returns (no SendGrid cancel, no delete). The only place that actually cancels SendGrid + deletes the row is the new block in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only processes `cancelled: true` reminders whose `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. Therefore a reminder far in the future remains in SendGrid as an active scheduled send until the final hour, and if `scheduleEmailReminders` is not invoked during that window, the SendGrid send would still fire despite the booking/workflow being cancelled/rescheduled.
